Name keys for matching people across Part VII rosters

Source: R/names.R
name_keys.Rd

Parses each distinct name once and returns its parts and its matching key. Parsed names are cached for the R session, so later calls with the same names are fast.

Usage

name_keys(
  x,
  method = c("canonical", "simple"),
  prefixes = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  workers = getOption("npmerger.name_workers", 1L)
)

name_key(
  x,
  method = c("canonical", "simple"),
  prefixes = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  workers = getOption("npmerger.name_workers", 1L)
)

name_keys_preload(keys, prefixes = NULL)

name_keys_cached(prefixes = NULL)

name_parser_id()

Arguments

x

Character vector of raw names.

method

"canonical" or "simple". "canonical" needs the peopleparser package; without it, "simple" is used with a warning.

prefixes

Titles and post-nominals to strip, passed to peopleparser::parse_name(). Defaults to peopleparser's own list.

verbose

Report progress for large batches.

workers

Number of R processes for parsing, passed to peopleparser::parse_names(). The default, 1, parses in this R session whatever future::plan() is set. With more, that many workers are started for the call, and the call stops if any of them loads a different peopleparser build than this session (for example after a reinstall mid-build). Set the default for a session with options(npmerger.name_workers = 8).

keys

A table from name_keys().

Value

A data.table with one row per distinct input name: PERSON_NAME, FIRST_NAME, MIDDLE_NAME, LAST_NAME, FIRST_CANONICAL, CANONICAL_RULE (self, spelling, nickname, ambiguous), and PERSON_KEY. With "simple", the parsed columns are NA.

Details

With method = "canonical", names are parsed with peopleparser::parse_name() and peopleparser::nickname_lookup(), and the key is the canonical first name plus the parsed last name. Nicknames resolve to their formal name (BOB -> ROBERT), and spelling variants to their most common spelling (DIANNE -> DIANE). Names whose nickname is ambiguous keep their own spelling (KATHY, or PAT without a gendered salutation). With method = "simple", the key is person_key().

Functions

  • name_key(): The key alone, one per element of x (NA for names that cannot be keyed).

  • name_keys_preload(): Add already-parsed names to the session cache, for example a name_keys table saved in a project database.

  • name_keys_cached(): Every name parsed this session (for saving).

  • name_parser_id(): The installed peopleparser that parsed the names: its version and commit (or build time, for a local install). Saved parses are reused only by the same parser.

See also

name_match_basis() for why two names share a key.

Examples

people <- c( "Robert Smith", "BOB SMITH", "Dr. Robert J. Smith PhD",
             "Kathy Lee", "MRS PAT JONES" )

if ( requireNamespace( "peopleparser", quietly = TRUE ) ) {
  name_keys( people )
}
